critical: ch09-s06/s07: GPU speed is one of the bible's contested claims (sec. 9: present both sides; E6 settled view: 'not against 8 JS workers'), but the film only sets the GPU search against RegExp on ONE thread (8-28 ms vs 11-15 ms, 2.1 s vs 11 ms). JS13's other side is never stated: against JavaScript in 8 workers RegExp is faster (1.9-6.7 ms vs the GPU's 4.5-5.2 ms back to back; the GPU takes 2-8x as long after a pause). The '1 of 18 cores' review in s07 makes viewers think the shown numbers are the corrected fair comparison, yet JS11's RegExp figures are still one thread.

ch08-s02: the nameCard caption 'not Cheng' asserts something the record does not say. LB02 and bible E4 say only that the participants of the 'design conversation' are not named, so the beliefs are not ATTRIBUTABLE to Cheng. In a one-author repo he may well have been in that conversation. Saying he wasn't is an unsupported negative claim about a living person.

ch02-s06: 'Yet eighty-three years later, someone wrote a network's weights by hand again.' The word 'again' says nobody did it in between. The film itself contradicts that in ch06-s12: Siegelmann & Sontag hand-built nets in 1992. The bible (FR22) also notes RASP/Tracr-style program-to-network work, which the repo's lab notes cite (RASP, Merrill & Sabharwal, Percepta). This is a factual overclaim in the film's thesis line.

issues.where: ch02-s03 L3 'Anything unbounded, like time, has to come from outside.'
issues.problem: This is not in FR07/FR08 or Q141, and it is technically muddled. A finite automaton already handles input sequences of any length over time; what a finite net lacks is unbounded MEMORY. Kleene's Q141 mentions time only as quantized ticks. The visual (a crank outside the dial) and the ch06-s12 payoff present this as Kleene's insight.
issues.fix: Reword as the film's own reading and fix the concept: 'A finite net can only remember so much. Anything unbounded has to come from outside.' In ch06-s12, frame the payoff with the repo's own comparison (FR25, Q127), which is already on screen, rather than as Kleene's claim.

issues.where: global: on-screen reading time (70 assemble warnings)
issues.problem: Many on-screen quotes don't stay up long enough to read (e.g. ch09-s03 152 chars at ~9.2 s of 14.2 s needed; ch08-s05 116 chars at 5.9 s of 11.2 s). A quote viewers can't finish reading misleads as surely as a misquote, and the film leans on its sources for credibility.
issues.fix: In the shots where the quote is the evidence (ch04-s15, ch08-s05, ch09-s03, ch09-s07, ch11-s03, ch11-s04), lengthen holdAfter or minDuration to the check's 'needed' figure, or trim to a shorter verbatim span from quotes.json.

strengths: Quote integrity is excellent: all 78 on-screen quotes are verbatim from quotes.json, attributed at the right level ('the docs', 'the learned gallery's README', 'Cheng Lou, as quoted in the lab's notes', 'a Hacker News commenter'). Cheng is quoted only where the repo marks his words.

Every worked example is real and checks under Math.fround: the 4.5 -> 11 and 16,777,222 -> 8 failures, the boolean atom's tie to even, the 1732 px column count, the FP32 row sums, the spring step, the valve gradients.

Honest scoping throughout: 'in the repo's tests' for bit-identity, 'a float64 copy' for the 359 px drift, 'one machine' and dates on every timing, '(derived)' on derived figures, 'an echo, not a citation' for Kleene, 'context: the repo cites none of this work' on every history card.

The ternary deep dive is a model of accuracy-as-drama. It separates the README's integer-only trick, the false-grid case (11 again, validator objects) and the sign cascade (correct at 4.5). That avoids the bible's banned 'emitCompare is always wrong at 4.5'.

The AI-tooling disclosure in ch08-s07 is even-handed: Claude Code credited, the earlier Codex agent named, 'This film was written with Claude' said plainly, and mistakes and catches framed as one process under Cheng's direction, as the bible asks.

Contested matters are mostly handled with care: Bitter Lesson vs Brooks, the frog paper's 'refutation came later', snap vs carry as a design choice, 'fully differentiable' doubted by the repo itself, TOML's failure stated with the README's own caveat that it 'does not say that training cannot work there'.
The record's silences are respected: 'The record doesn't say why. So we won't guess.' (August), 'no public discussion of the lab ... found', and the bison drawer left open.
